resources.n: EPSDT - the rule that overturns a "no" for anyone under 21
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: For any Medicaid member under 21, a plan CANNOT say no just because a service is not in its coverage policy or goes past a policy limit. It has to run a separate EPSDT review and approve the service if it would correct or improve the condition, keep it from getting worse, or prevent another condition. Under 21 there are also no copays, no limit on how often a service is given, no limit on how many services in one day, and services can be delivered where the child actually is, including school and community settings.
resources.h: The PROVIDER has to make the request and has to explain in writing how the service will help. Ask them to use the words "EPSDT review" in the request.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in both the Vaya and Healthy Blue member handbooks. This is the strongest single lever in this guide: therapy hours, ABA, equipment, private duty nursing, anything the plan calls over the limit. If they still deny after an EPSDT review, the clock is 60 days to appeal, 30 days for a decision, 72 hours if expedited.

resources.n: When the plan denies something - the clock, and the free help
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: 60 days from the date on the denial letter to file an appeal. The plan then has 30 days to decide. Ask for an EXPEDITED appeal and it drops to 72 hours if waiting would harm health, and the provider can request it too. If a service the child ALREADY HAS is being cut or stopped, ask for continuation of benefits within 10 days of the notice and it keeps running until the appeal is decided. If the appeal is lost, 120 days to ask for a State Fair Hearing. The Mediation Network calls within 5 business days to offer a free, optional mediation before the hearing.
resources.h: NC Medicaid Ombudsman 877-201-3750, free and independent of the plan. Mediation Network of NC 336-461-3300. Office of Administrative Hearings 984-236-1860.
resources.t: Added 4 Aug 2026, verified in both handbooks. TWO CAUTIONS. First, the NC Medicaid Ombudsman is NOT the Long-Term Care Ombudsman at Land of Sky: different program, different job. Second, if a family asks for continuation of benefits and then LOSES the appeal, the plan is allowed to bill them for what it paid during the appeal, though only with NC Medicaid approval first. Say that out loud before a family chooses it.

resources.n: 🎯 1915(i) services - Medicaid respite without waiting out Innovations
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: The services that replaced (b)(3) on 1 July 2023. Five of them: RESPITE, Community Living and Support, Individual and Transitional Support, Community Transition, and Supported Employment. The thing that makes this reachable is that 1915(i) does NOT require an institutional level of care, which Innovations does. Qualifying conditions are a serious mental health condition, a severe substance use disorder, an I/DD, or a TBI. Sitting on the Innovations Registry of Unmet Needs does not disqualify anyone, and using 1915(i) does NOT cost a family its place in that line. Being found eligible for 1915(i) also makes you eligible for Tailored Care Management. Call Vaya 1-800-962-9003 and ask the Tailored Care Manager for a 1915(i) independent assessment. It goes to the state; if eligible, the care manager writes the service into the care plan and submits it for prior authorisation.
resources.t: Respite, Medicaid, Vaya, I/DD, Mental health, Free | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on medicaid.ncdhhs.gov, page last modified 8 Jan 2026. Say "1915(i)", NOT "(b)(3)": the old name was retired and asking for it now can produce a false no. NOT available on Standard Plans (Healthy Blue, WellCare, UnitedHealthcare, AmeriHealth Caritas, Carolina Complete), so a Standard Plan family with a qualifying condition may need to ask the Enrollment Broker to move to the Tailored Plan first. Anyone who ALREADY holds an Innovations or TBI Waiver slot is not eligible, because those waivers already cover it. This is the widest respite door in this file for a child with a mental health diagnosis and no I/DD.

resources.n: 🎯 In Lieu of Services - the alternatives to residential, PRTF and the ER
resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Vaya-approved substitutes for standard Medicaid services. Each one is a step DOWN from a placement or an ER trip, and families are almost never told they exist. For children and youth: HIGH-FIDELITY WRAPAROUND (in place of residential level II), FAMILY-CENTERED TREATMENT delivered in the home (in place of a level III group home), CHILD ACT (in place of a PRTF), ENHANCED CRISIS RESPONSE (for a youth at risk of the ER, or already in one and unable to go home), IN-HOME THERAPY (in place of intensive in-home or MST), OUTPATIENT PLUS (when plain outpatient is not enough), RAPID CARE (up to 24 hours in a facility instead of the ER or an admission), and TRANSITIONAL YOUTH SERVICES for ages 16 to 21 (in place of residential). For adults: long-term community supports, dual-diagnosis ACT, first-episode psychosis ACT, and a crisis risk assessment at a behavioural health urgent care instead of the ER. Ask the provider or care manager to request the service BY NAME. A family can also call Vaya 1-800-962-9003 and ask which of these are contracted near them.

resources.d: Two home-delivered meals a day for up to seven days, so 14 meals, in the month after discharge from a qualifying inpatient hospital stay. A psychiatric admission counts. No cost. Delivered by Mom's Meals. Ask the care manager BEFORE a planned admission, during the stay, or straight after discharge. The window closes 30 days after the discharge date.

THE HANDBOOK OMITS TWO CONDITIONS that will get a family denied: you must be participating in Tailored Care Management, and you must not already be eligible for meal delivery through the Innovations Waiver. Also, an ER visit and an outpatient surgery performed at a hospital do NOT count as a qualifying stay. The Nov 2025 handbook says only "fourteen meals" and "within one month". Best use here is a parent coming home after a psychiatric admission or a birth, into a house with no groceries.

resources.t: Free, Vaya, Medicaid, Spanish / bilingual, Adult education | Added 4 Aug 2026, verified on vayahealth.com. The exam fee is the wall most people hit, and this pays it. Two-generation: a parent finishing a GED moves the household income ceiling, not just their own resume. Also on the Vaya perks list and not given its own row here: a six-month WeightWatchers app voucher, for members 18+ with a BMI of 25 or higher, one per calendar year, requested through the Member and Recipient Portal with medical documentation.

Substance use ROUTINE: 48 HOURS. Well-child visit: 14 days if the child is under 6 months, 30 days if older. Adult preventive: 30 days. First prenatal visit: 14 days in the 1st or 2nd trimester, 5 DAYS in the 3rd trimester or a high-risk pregnancy. If a family is quoted a longer wait, call Vaya Member and Recipient Services 1-800-962-9003 and say the standard out loud. If nothing moves, file it as a grievance.

A grievance must be acknowledged in writing within 5 days and answered within 30. This is a number to hand the family so THEY can say it, not only something the FRP says on their behalf.

resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: On joining Vaya you can keep an OUT-OF-NETWORK provider for UP TO 180 DAYS if you are mid-course of treatment or have an ongoing condition, and the handbook names I/DD, a mental health diagnosis, substance use disorder and TBI as qualifying. More than 3 months pregnant: keep the provider through delivery plus 60 days postpartum. Pregnant and seeing a behavioural health provider: through delivery. A scheduled surgery or inpatient stay: through the procedure plus 90 days of follow-up. Terminally ill: for the rest of your life. Separately, a SECOND OPINION needs no prior authorisation, in network or out. Tell the care manager you want to keep the provider. They document it and start an Out-of-Network Agreement, roughly 3 business days. Or call 1-800-962-9003.

If a PCP leaves the network Vaya must tell the family in writing within 7 days, 15 days for any other provider. Continuity is a right here, not a favour, and a child should not have to restart a therapeutic relationship because the state redrew a map.

If a prescription needs prior authorisation, the pharmacy can dispense a 72-HOUR SUPPLY while it is decided, and the decision is due within 24 hours. It can also nominate a guardian in advance. It can stand alone or be combined with a health care power of attorney. It only takes effect once a doctor or eligible psychologist states in writing that you cannot make or communicate the decision, and you can change or revoke it at any time. Free forms at sosnc.gov/ahcdr. Registering with the NC Secretary of State makes it findable by a hospital at 2am. Vaya will help a member understand or obtain the documents: 1-800-962-9003.

resources.spd: Federally or publicly funded: a free qualified interpreter must be provided on request. Ask for one when you call.
resources.d: Under NC law a minor can consent, without a parent or guardian, to four things: treatment for sexually transmitted infections, services related to pregnancy, help with alcohol or other substance use, and help with emotional conditions. On top of that, no referral is needed for a first behavioural health or substance use assessment in any 12-month period, and none is ever needed for mobile crisis. Any Vaya network provider. resources.spd: Not stated in the source. Ask when you call. Their materials are English-only online.
resources.d: Church-based volunteer host families care for your children short term while you deal with a crisis. THE PARENT NEVER LOSES CUSTODY and can ask for the children home whenever they want. Contact stays open the whole time: visits, texts, FaceTime, phone calls. Average hosting is 4 to 6 weeks, range is one day to a year. Reasons families use it, in their own words: medical emergency, homelessness, an expected baby, a treatment or recovery programme, mental health care, and gaps between employment and childcare. Free. A Community Coach also works with the PARENT on the parent's own goals, and visits the host home within the first two days. Referral line 828-357-7075, Mon-Fri 9am-5pm. THIS IS NOT A 24/7 CRISIS LINE. As an FRP use the agency referral form at myvillageasheville.org/referrals, and call the line too, which is what they ask agency workers to do. Families can self-refer at myvillageasheville.org/support.
resources.t: Respite, Host home, Free, Faith-based, Voluntary, Pregnancy, Kids / 0-5 | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on myvillageasheville.org. SAY THIS TO THE FAMILY BEFORE YOU REFER: it is an explicitly Christian organisation working through local churches. They say themselves that a family's views do not need to match theirs to use the service, but a family deserves to know before they walk in, not after. Host families are volunteers, screened by application, home evaluation and safety checklist, fingerprinting and background checks, character references, interview and training. They are NOT DSS-licensed foster homes, and this is NOT a licensed placement. Because it is private and voluntary there is no DSS oversight and no Medicaid appeal route if something goes wrong. IT DOES NOT REPLACE A REPORT: if a safety concern meets the reporting threshold, report it. This was Alongside Families Asheville until 7 JULY 2025, when My Village Ministries took the site over with no programme change and no volunteer retraining. Sister chapter Elizabeth's House at My Village, Hickory, Catawba County, referral line 828-330-3494, runs the same model with a focus on pregnant and single mothers: only relevant if a family has ties out that way.

resources.n: 🎯 Play Talk & Grow - speech, feeding, AAC, takes Medicaid and Vaya
resources.d: Pediatric speech and language, birth to 18, in the clinic and inside some daycares and private schools. Not just articulation. They do AAC (talkers and communication boards), LAMP motor planning, Natural Language Acquisition for gestalt language processors and children who talk in scripts or echolalia, SPELLING TO COMMUNICATE for minimally speaking or unreliably speaking autistic kids, PROMPT for childhood apraxia, DIRFloortime, feeding and swallowing therapy (chewing, safe swallowing, expanding what a child will eat), literacy and dyslexia work, and stuttering. Parents sit IN the session and get coached, which is the part that makes it carry over at home. Neurodiversity-affirming and child-led by their own description: they do not use compliance-based methods. 18 Regent Park Blvd, Suite A, West Asheville 28806. Mon-Fri 8am-6pm by appointment. FREE consultation with an actual speech therapist first, and they check the family's benefits before anyone commits. Start at playtalkandgrow.com/get-started.
resources.t: Speech, Feeding, AAC, Autism, Medicaid, Vaya, Kids / 0-5, ESA+ | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on playtalkandgrow.com. This is the single most useful fact about them and it is not obvious from their site, because the intake form only offers Private Insurance or Self-Pay as tick-boxes: SAY MEDICAID OUT LOUD ON THE PHONE rather than trusting the form. PRICE CONFLICT ON THEIR OWN PAGE: the pricing table says $215 evaluation and $90 a session, the FAQ four inches below says $195 and $80. Ask which applies before the first appointment. They also take ESA+, HSA and FSA, and issue Superbills for out-of-network. Free extras worth knowing: caregiver video tutorials, public webinars, and THE ASHEVILLE LIST at playtalkandgrow.com/the-asheville-list, their own directory of neurodiversity-affirming local providers, which is a genuinely useful cross-check on this guide.

resources.n: Campfire Behavioral Health (Campfire ABA) - no waitlist, Spanish on site
resources.d: ABA for children and young adults aged 2 to 21 with autism and other intellectual disabilities, 1:1, in two-hour sessions. Founded 2023 by a BCBA who is also the parent of a child with level 3 autism, moved to Asheville 2025, and deliberately stays small. Separate ADULT service for people over 18 who are on the NC INNOVATIONS WAIVER. Also: an Outdoor Adventures partner programme that runs sessions in the mountains instead of a clinic room, telehealth for rural families, and pediatric neurofeedback through Asheville Neurowellness. THEY SAY THEY HAVE NO WAITLIST, which in this county is the whole story. 15 Henrietta St, Asheville 28801 per the Asheville Chamber listing. Their own site gives no street address, only 'Asheville', so confirm the address when you book. Phone (253) 349-6925, open 9am-5pm. Free consultation offered. Se habla Español, on-site interpreter, Iliana Guardado, herself a parent of an autistic child.
resources.t: Autism, ABA, I/DD, Innovations, Spanish / bilingual, Telehealth | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on campfireaba.info. TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE YOU SEND A FAMILY. First, FUNDING IS UNCLEAR ON THEIR OWN SITE: the 'insurance and funding sources we currently work with' panel lists six entries and every single one reads Private Pay, while the FAQ two screens down says most sessions are covered by insurance. Medicaid is never named. NC Medicaid does cover ABA for autism under EPSDT through the Tailored Plan, so ask directly whether they bill Vaya, and get the answer before the family gets attached. Second, the phone number is a 253 area code, which is Washington State, not 828. That is not a red flag by itself for a practice that relocated here in 2025, but a family who is screening unknown numbers will let it ring out, so warn them. SEPARATELY: ABA is contested. Many autistic adults and neurodiversity-affirming clinicians object to it, and other providers in this guide, including Play Talk & Grow, position themselves explicitly against compliance-based methods. This is a real disagreement among reasonable people, not a settled question. A parent gets to weigh it. Give them both sides and the question already written on the IX tab: ask any provider how they handle a child saying no.

resources.n: ⚠️ Campfire Community School - opens 20 Aug 2026, read the funding note first
resources.d: A new private school in Asheville for neurodivergent students, first day 20 AUGUST 2026, enrolling now. Every student gets a 1:1 behaviour technician and an individual learning plan built by special education consultants and BCBAs. Learning is built around movement, sensory activity and games rather than desk work. Term dates published: parent reviews 6 Nov 2026 and 5 Feb 2027, breaks 23-27 Nov and 21 Dec to 1 Jan, spring break 5-9 Apr 2027, last day 11 Jun 2027. Email info@campfireaba.com to ask about enrolment. No street address, grade range, class size or tuition figure is published anywhere on their site. Ask for all four in writing.
resources.t: Autism, School, ESA+, Opportunity Scholarship, Private school, Deadline | Added 17 Aug 2026, verified on campfireaba.info. FOUR THINGS A FAMILY MUST KNOW BEFORE THEY MOVE A CHILD. (1) THE OPPORTUNITY SCHOLARSHIP WINDOW FOR 2026-27 CLOSED AT 5PM ON 14 AUGUST 2026, four days before this row was written, so a family reading 'apply for Opportunity/ESA+' on the school's page today has already missed that one for this year. ESA+ has its own timeline: check k12.ncseaa.edu, do not assume. (2) ESA+ REQUIRES AN ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION FROM A NORTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SCHOOL ISSUED IN THE LAST THREE YEARS. So the free school evaluation on the IX tab is not an alternative to this money, it is the DOOR to it: request it in writing from Buncombe County Schools EC and the clock starts. Awards run roughly $9,000 to $17,000. (3) ASK WHETHER THEY ARE A DIRECT PAYMENT SCHOOL OR A REIMBURSEMENT SCHOOL. A reimbursement school means the FAMILY PAYS TUITION UP FRONT and claims it back. No Child First family can front a year of private school tuition. Also confirm they are registered with DNPE and with NCSEAA, because a brand new school may not be yet, and without both the money cannot follow the child. (4) MOVING TO A PRIVATE SCHOOL GIVES UP THE IEP. Under IDEA the individual entitlement to a free appropriate public education belongs to children enrolled in public school. A privately enrolled child may get a services plan, which is a much weaker thing, decided by the district and shared out across all private-school children. This is the trade-off nobody mentions in the brochure and it is not reversible mid-year. It may still be the right call for a child who is suffering in their classroom. It is the family's call, made with the facts.
